source.title: When Safety Routing Breaks: Understanding Alignment Fragility under Benign Fine-Tuning
source.authors: Yi-Tong Guo; Xiaoyi Chen; Si-Yuan Zhang; Xiao-Feng Wang; Hai-Xu Tang

record.file_problem: None apparent; the supplied text contains the paper and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports results about refusal fragility and an output-routing account, but it does not test the difference-in-means residual direction or any of the listed claim versions. Its intervention is benign fine-tuning, and its activation patching transfers whole residual states rather than ablating or adding the claimed direction.
record.gate_note: The study does not find a harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction, project such a direction out, or add it. It does not test jailbreak suppression of that direction or the existence of a removable direction across training regimes. Rows below record adjacent findings about refusal behavior and routing; they are not evidence for or against V1–V8 as specified.
record.test_reason: The study cites Arditi et al. (2024) only in related work. It never computes a difference-in-means refusal direction, ablates or adds one, or edits weights along one. Its methods are benign fine-tuning, block-wise Fisher spectra, logit-lens refusal/compliance token margins, and whole residual-state patching between checkpoints. None of these measures what V1–V8 name. The logit-lens and prefix results (refusal signal survives fine-tuning) sit near V5 but do not separate a harmfulness judgment from a refusal decision. The DPO/SFT comparisons sit near V7 but say nothing about whether a single removable direction exists.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also conclude three further points. Gradient conflict modulates the severity of collapse but is not necessary for it (random and low-conflict subsets also break safety). About 10–50 safety examples restore refusal. LoRA and ASAM mitigate early collapse, but their protection fades by 5000 samples.
record.recipe_differences: The study does not use the original difference-in-means direction, projection ablation, or direction addition. It studies benign fine-tuning, block-wise Fisher geometry, logit-lens read-outs, and cross-checkpoint residual-state patching.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported safety degradation varies with model family, alignment setting, benign dataset, fine-tuning size, and fine-tuning method. The paper reports weaker early collapse under LoRA and ASAM than full SFT, with mitigation weakening at larger data scales.

fits_no_version.finding: Aligned Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-7B models start at 0% HEx-PHI ASR. After 100 benign Alpaca examples, ASR rises to 59.6–85.7%. A DPO-aligned Llama rises to 66.96%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign utility fine-tuning on as few as 100 examples largely removes refusal in SFT- and DPO-aligned chat models.

fits_no_version.finding: A fixed 'I'm sorry' prefix lowers post-fine-tuning ASR (85.70→34.85; 59.60→2.12). Final-layer residual-state patching restores 96.9% of the refusal margin, and the reverse patch flips it negative.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: After benign fine-tuning, refusal is suppressed but recoverable, and final-layer computation controls the refusal/compliance switch.

fits_no_version.finding: Safety Fisher is more concentrated than utility Fisher (top-1 0.491 vs 0.271). After FT-100, final-layer safety sharpness rises 11.2×, versus 1.2× for utility.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign fine-tuning selectively re-sharpens late-layer curvature that governs refusal.

fits_no_version.finding: MMLU falls after FT-100, by much more for Llama (about 14–16 points) than for Qwen (about 3–5 points).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Utility loss from small benign fine-tuning is smaller than the safety loss and depends on the model.

record.problems: The central causal patching result is a refusal-compliance margin rather than a behavioral refusal rate, and it patches whole residual states rather than an identified direction. The paper reports two random seeds for many behavioral results; Fisher estimates use five seeds with confidence intervals shown in a figure. The authors note that the study is limited to mid-scale LLaMA-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-7B models and is English-centric.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted ASR results for the unaligned instruct baselines, LoRA and ASAM conditions, Dolly fine-tuning, gradient-conflict sampling, recovery by safety-example fine-tuning, and Wildchat/StrongReject evaluations. These results concern benign fine-tuning and safety recovery rather than any of V1–V8; the selected rows preserve the principal aligned-model ASR, DPO, prefix, patching, Fisher, and utility findings.

untested.parts: No difference-in-means direction; no directional ablation or addition; no capability check under such interventions.
No jailbreak analysis in terms of a refusal direction; no adversarial training against ablation.
Fisher top-k concentration is parameter-space curvature, not a test of multiple or affine refusal directions in activations.
No separate probe or intervention on harmfulness judgment versus refusal. The logit-lens refusal-token signal is not a harmfulness representation.
No cross-lingual, cross-model or base-to-instruct direction transfer.
Compares SFT-aligned (Align-256, Align-10k) and DPO-aligned fragility, but never tests whether a removable direction exists under each regime.

record.verdict_notes: The study is adjacent to the refusal-direction literature but tests no version. The reader's 'discusses' is changed to 'cites_only', because Arditi et al. appears only in related work and is never argued with. All row links stay 'none'.

versions.untested_parts: No difference-in-means direction, all-layer/all-position ablation, direction addition, or evaluation of other abilities under those interventions.
No test of whether attacks suppress the claimed direction or whether training against its ablation adds robustness.
Fisher concentration and residual-state patching do not test whether refusal is represented by an affine set, cone, or multiple refusal directions.
No separate measurement or intervention on harmfulness judgment versus refusal decision.
No cross-language transfer or transfer of a refusal direction between base and instruct models.
The paper compares alignment settings and SFT/DPO fragility, but does not test whether training determines the existence of a removable direction.
